content: 1. Infigratinib affects the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 2. Both inotuzumab and voriconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and monitor electrolytes before and after initiation of any QTc-prolonging drug, and periodically during treatment as clinically indicated. 3. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of irinotecan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of irinotecan liposomal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Both isoflurane and voriconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Itraconazole increases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of ivosidenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least 5 half-lives of the inhibitor. 8. Both ivosidenib and voriconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of QTc-prolonging drugs with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. 9. Ivosidenib decreases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sensitive CYP2C9 substrates with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect of these drugs. 10. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of ketamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of larotrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior larotrectinib dose once the inhibitor is discontinued for 3-5 half-lives. 12. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of lefamulin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 13. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of lemborexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 14. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of leniolisib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of lorlatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lorlatinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase to the previous lorlatinib dose after 3 plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 17. Lorlatinib decreases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of lurbinectedin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After the inhibitor is discontinued for 5 half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to the dose used before coadministration. 19. Both macimorelin and voriconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Macimorelin causes an increase of ~11 msec in the corrected QT interval. Avoid coadministration with QT-prolonging drugs to reduce the risk of torsade de pointes-type ventricular tachycardia. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 20. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of macitentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of medroxyprogesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of mefloquine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. There is potential for increased toxicity. Avoid coadministration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 23. Voriconazole and methyl aminolevulinate increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Each drug may increase the photosensitizing effect of the other. 24. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of intranasal midazolam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors causes higher systemic exposure to midazolam, potentially prolonging sedation. 25. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of midostaurin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, monitor midostaurin for increased risk of adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 26. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of nelfinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of neratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Nirmatrelvir decreases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of voriconazole and low-dose ritonavir (e.g., 100 mg q12hr) due to induction of CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 enzymes by ritonavir. 30. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of voriconazole and low-dose ritonavir (e.g., 100 mg q12hr) due to induction of CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 enzymes by ritonavir. 31. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of nirogacestat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of olaparib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) PO BID. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 33. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of omaveloxolone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. 34. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir decrease the level or effect of voriconazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. This combination is not recommended unless the benefit-to-risk ratio justifies the use of voriconazole. 36. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of ondansetron by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both ondansetron and voriconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid with congenital long QT syndrome; ECG monitoring is recommended with concomitant QT-prolonging medications, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 37. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of osimertinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 38. Both oxaliplatin and voriconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Voriconazole increases levels of oxycodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Oxycodone dose reduction may be warranted when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of palbociclib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of palbociclib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 41. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of palovarotene by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Both voriconazole and panobinostat increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat significantly prolongs the QT interval. Its prescribing information states that use with QTc-prolonging drugs is not recommended. 43. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of pazopanib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of pazopanib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible; if coadministration is necessary, decrease the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 44. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of pemigatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose (refer to drug monograph dosage modifications). After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives, resume the previous pemigatinib dose. 45. Both pentamidine and voriconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Pentobarbital decreases levels of voriconazole by increasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 47. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of pexidartinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose (refer to drug monograph dosage modifications). After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives, resume the previous pexidartinib dose. 48. Phenytoin decreases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of pimavanserin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Decrease the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 50. Both pimozide and voriconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of pirtobrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current pirtobrutinib dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Once the inhibitor is discontinued for 5 half-lives, resume pirtobrutinib at the dose taken before initiating the inhibitor. 52. Both voriconazole and pitolisant increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Voriconazole increases levels of pomalidomide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Voriconazole increases levels of ponatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Decrease the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily if coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided. 55. Posaconazole increases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 56. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of pralsetinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Primidone decreases levels of voriconazole by increasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 58. Both procainamide and voriconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of ranolazine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 60. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of red yeast rice by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice may increase creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis, as it contains monacolin K (identical to lovastatin). 61. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of repotrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 62. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of ribociclib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Inform patients to avoid pomegranate or grapefruit products. Ribociclib increases voriconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. 63. Rifabutin decreases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
